## Rubric summary

The rubric uses four performance levels: Unsatisfactory, Needs Improvement, Meets Expectations, and Exceeds Expectations.

| Criterion | Meets Expectations | Exceeds Expectations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Appearance and theme | Coherent, organized layout; backing and borders; tape concealed; mostly clean edges | Creative, polished theme and consistently clean construction |
| Visual appeal | Presentation attracts the reader's attention | Includes a distinctive visual or three-dimensional feature |
| Legibility and space | Readable typed or die-cut information; some space may remain underused | Creative, readable presentation that makes fuller use of the board |
| CEM anchor alignment | Content connects clearly to a CEM anchor | Connection is purposeful, thorough, and impactful |
| Information depth | Informative content with some depth | Substantive material that serves readers with different prior knowledge |
| Interaction | Clear, engaging interactive component | Innovative and especially engaging interaction |
| Spelling and grammar | Few or no errors | Error-free work with close attention to detail |

The lower levels identify missing or inconsistent themes, weak presentation, hard-to-read text, poor spacing, incomplete anchor alignment, shallow information, weak or absent interaction, and language errors. Consult the original rubric for the precise evaluation language.

Meet the Residential Life Team

Welcome from Associate Director, Dr. Domonique Crosby

Hi RAs,

 

First things first, thank you!

 

Thank you for saying yes to this role. Thank you for your willingness to lead, to support your peers, and to be a part of something bigger than yourself. The Resident Advisor position is one of the most impactful student leadership roles on campus, and we do not take your commitment lightly.

 

Whether this is your first year as an RA or you are returning with some experience under your belt, know that your presence matters. You help shape the residential experience for hundreds of students. You are often the first person they turn to with questions, with concerns, and in moments of celebration or challenge. That is no small thing.

 

This manual is here to help you along the way. It is a guide to the policies, practices, and resources you will need to feel grounded and confident in your role. It will not have every answer, but it will point you in the right direction. Keep it close and do not be afraid to ask questions as you go.

 

I want you to hear this clearly: we see you, and we appreciate you!! Your time, energy, compassion, and care are what make our communities feel like home. It is not always easy, but it is deeply meaningful, and you are not doing it alone. You have a team behind you that believes in you and is here to support you every step of the way.

 

Best,

Dr. Domonique Crosby

Associate Director for Residential Education

Mission

We seek to provide a safe environment that encourages learning and personal growth in an inclusive community that empowers and challenges our residents. We continually strive to improve our services to meet the needs of our students and guests and reflect the high standards of WashU.

About Being an RA
This is the page for job descriptions, expectations, communication standards, work agreement, evaluation material, and accountability information. 

Communication Standards
Monitor Communication Platforms Daily 

Check Microsoft Teams and university email accounts at least once per day to stay up to date on important information from supervisors and the Residential Life department.

Respond to messages and requests in a timely manner, ideally within 24 hours on business days.

Media and Public Statements 

RAs must not speak to the media (including student publications, local news outlets, or online platforms) as a representative of the Residential Life department or the university.

If contacted by media, RAs should refer all inquiries to the Residential Life Center (reslife@wustl.edu) and let their supervisor know of the request. 

 

Communication with Residents 

Use Microsoft Teams as the primary method of communication with residents, when appropriate.

Maintain professional tone and boundaries in all written and verbal communication.

When necessary, follow up in person or via email for more formal or confidential matters.

Professional Conduct and Confidentiality 

All communication, whether digital or in person, should reflect respect, inclusion, and professionalism.

Do not share confidential student information or internal Residential Life matters outside of authorized channels.

Escalation and Reporting 

If unsure about how to handle a communication (e.g., media request, sensitive resident issue), consult your supervising Residential Community Director before responding.

Report any concerning communications or incidents promptly through the proper channels.

Gather all information from the reporting source: 

Name and relationship to student in need of wellness check   

Gather all information related to the student and wellness check: name, age, reason for wellness check (i.e. illness, injury, missing class, haven’t been seen or heard from)

Do try to determine what areas are causing concern (academics, finances, relationships, etc.)

Do let the resident know that people care about them, that you care and that you don't want them to commit suicide. 

Do help the student determine a positive course of action by helping them assess the situation and by identifying other options. 

Do discuss available people and resources that can help. Explain that TIMELYCARE needs to talk to the student via phone. Let them know that the service is free and that many students use it. The RCD needs to be present when the conversation with TimelyCare occurs

Do find out what the resident's plans are for the rest of the evening and the next few days. Try to encourage them to join you for a floor program, meals, etc.

Follow up with your RCD or the RCD On-Call immediately after the interaction.

RA Duty Phone Expectations 

Tuesday, January 07, 2025 

4:28 PM 

  

🔁 Duty Phone Turn-in Protocol 

Location: The duty phone should be placed in the appropriate desk drawer in either the RLC or the Village Office no earlier that 8:30am on weekdays and no earlier than 1:30pm on weekends (for the South 40) 

Timely Transfer: There should never be a gap in coverage, if there is no one at the desk when turning in the phone, either wait for someone to get there or notify the RCD on duty 

  

📱 Phone Care and Preparedness 

Keep It Charged: Always return the phone fully charged and ensure it's charged throughout your shift. Place the phone on charge when you return it to the desk as well. 

Volume On, Not Silent: The phone must always have the ringer and vibrate on at an audible level (not on silent or vibrate-only). 

Physically With You: The duty phone must remain on your person or within close reach at all times during your duty shift. Never left unattended or given to a non-RA. 

  

📞 Call and Text Response Expectations 

Immediate Response: Calls must be answered immediately unless you’re responding to an emergency (in which case call back as soon as safely possible). 

Professional Demeanor: Answer with a professional and consistent greeting (e.g., “Hi, this is the RA on duty, how can I help you?”). 

Follow-Up: Record incidents or follow up as needed per protocol. 

  

⛔ Prohibited Uses 

Personal Use Forbidden: No personal texts, calls, social media, or app usage on the duty phone. Even to other current or former RAs. 

No Sharing: Do not lend the duty phone to anyone else, including other RAs not on duty. 

RA Duty Number: The duty phone numbers should NEVER be share with residents 

  

💬 Backup Plan 

If You're Late/Unavailable: Notify RCD on call in advance. It is your responsibility to find a replacement or coverage when needed. 

Phone Malfunctions: Report any issues with the phone (e.g., battery failure, cracked screen, network problems) immediately to the RCD on call.
